description: Source-adaptive professional mastering intents. Genre models define context and safety envelopes; presets define aesthetic direction and maximum permissions; waveform analysis decides actual processing.

architecture.principle: Analyze first. Genre provides context. Preset provides aesthetic intent. DSP applies only justified processing. Re-analyze and reject regressions.

pop.description: Modern pop: vocal clarity, controlled low end, polished extension, moderate-to-high density.

rock.description: Rock/metal: punch, guitar density and transient preservation without upper-mid fatigue.

edm.description: EDM: powerful controlled sub/kick, high density, safe width and clean transient loudness.

hiphop.description: Hip-hop/trap/drill: 808 authority, vocal center, transient punch and restrained low-mid buildup.

rnb.description: R&B/soul: warm low mids, intimate vocal, smooth presence and polished air.

acoustic.description: Acoustic/singer-songwriter: natural tone, room depth and transient/dynamic preservation.

classical.description: Classical/orchestral: preserve macro/micro dynamics, natural spectral balance and stereo realism.

jazz.description: Jazz: preserve articulation, instrument timbre, space and meaningful dynamic contrast.

country.description: Country/americana: vocal intelligibility, acoustic/transient definition and controlled warmth.

reggae.description: Reggae/dancehall: deep bass authority, clean low mids, stable center and relaxed top end.

latin.description: Latin/reggaeton: punchy kick/bass, vocal clarity, percussion definition and energetic but safe top end.

afrobeats.description: Afrobeats: rhythmic low-end definition, open mids, vocal clarity and lively percussion without glare.

lofi.description: Lo-fi: intentionally warm/dark coloration while protecting intelligibility and avoiding uncontrolled mud.

podcast.description: Speech/content: intelligibility, stable level, low noise/mud and mono-safe translation.
